summary.headline: Solarworld Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 77% YoY to Rs 2,244 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5.9% and management now targets 6-7% for FY27.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was reported as Rs 2,244 crore (transcript figure, likely a transcription error for a much smaller base), up about 77% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 15.2 crore (5.9% margin) versus Rs 18.1 crore a year earlier. Half-year revenue was Rs 412 crore (about 100% YoY) with H1 EBITDA of Rs 35.8 crore (8.3%) and PAT of Rs 13.7 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to metal price spikes on fixed-price PSU contracts won before the spike, with LOAs delayed by 4-5 months. Order book stood at Rs 3,856 crore as of October 31, 2026, with BESS contributing about Rs 1,138 crore.

segments.name: Solar ETC and O&M
segments.commentary: Order book of Rs 2,718 crore as of Oct 31, 2026. Management expects this to be about 12-14 hundred crore revenue in FY28, including module and cell lines bundled in.

segments.name: BESS ETC and BESS factory
segments.commentary: BESS orders of 582 MW AC and about 1.3 GWh from RRVUNL, GUVNL and NTPC. Fully automated BESS factory commissioned, with about 1 GW of capacity covered by orders. Management targets Rs 1,500-1,800 crore BESS revenue in FY28 and about 600 containers.

segments.name: Solar module manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.5 GW ALMM-listed module plant is operational; 5 GW junction box line has commenced operation. Management expects 60-70% internal utilisation of the planned solar cell capacity.

segments.name: Solar cell JV (Madhya Pradesh)
segments.commentary: 2.4 GW TOPCon cell facility at Narmadapuram via JV; targeted commercial production June 2027 (management also said second quarter of next year). First equity tranche of about Rs 26.8 crore paid on October 30, 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue of Rs 1,600-1,700 crore and EBITDA margin of 6-7% (management said it still targets 5-6% in one answer), with PAT tax of about Rs 80-90 crore.
FY27: about Rs 1,100-1,200 crore of order execution in the year, with about Rs 2,600 crore of order book carried into FY28.
FY28: revenue of about Rs 3,000 crore, with BESS at Rs 1,500-1,800 crore and solar ETC at Rs 1,200-1,400 crore; tax of about Rs 200-220 crore. Management called FY28 a 'bumper year'.
Medium term (2-3 years): revenue target of about Rs 5,000 crore.
Solar cell and module margins guided at 15-20% going forward; BESS IPP projects targeted at minimum IRR of about 16%; NTPC BESS project EBITDA/PAT of about 10%.
Management said the board will return to shareholders in the current quarter with short-term actions on shareholder value; buyback was raised by an investor and not confirmed.
capex_capacity: Fully automated BESS manufacturing facility commissioned with KUKA robotics; about 1 GW of capacity covered by orders.
1.5 GW ALMM-listed solar module plant is operational; 5 GW junction box line has commenced operation.
2.4 GW solar cell JV at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh; commercial production targeted June 2027. Some cell equipment still required from China and pre-approval for export is needed.
Management is evaluating a 2 GWh lithium-ion cell plant in India; PLI application withdrawn; decision expected by end-December 2026.
Management said it will not scale manufacturing beyond what supports ETC business, and is not aiming to become a major manufacturer.
demand_pricing: Metal price spike (copper, aluminium, steel) and rupee move between Oct 2025 and Jan 2026 hit margins on fixed-price PSU contracts (NTPC, SJVN, NHPC); no pass-through in PSU tenders, while some private contracts do have pass-through.
Management said about Rs 400 crore of procurement was done in H1 and it delayed buying to wait for prices to ease; BESS IRRs had fallen to 8-9% and were said to have doubled after the delay.
BESS: lithium carbonate fell from about 200,000 yuan/t to about 90,000 yuan/t over six months; utility BESS market estimated at 350-400 GWh over the next 5-6 years in India.

Solar cell prices at about Rs 12-12.5 per cell vs manufacturing cost of about Rs 6-6.5 per management; module competition is intense with about 200 GW of capacity against about 50 GW expected installation.
Pricing: Management said the new orders (about Rs 1,500 crore per year) were won at higher prices and should give higher margins if metal prices normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Profitability roadmap for the next 12 months, 2 years and 3 years, and revised PAT guidance versus earlier IPO-stage guidance of Rs 200-300 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue of Rs 1,600-1,700 crore at 6-7% margin implies PAT tax of Rs 80-90 crore; FY28 revenue around Rs 3,000 crore with tax of Rs 200-220 crore; management called FY28 a 'bumper year'.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and shareholder value given the share price decline since IPO, including buyback.
qa_highlights.answer: Board is evaluating short-term actions and will come back to shareholders probably in the current quarter; no buyback was confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin change and raw material cost; whether hedging or pass-through exists.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost of materials will normalise to last year's percentage of revenue in the coming H2 as projects are executed; LCs hedge imported items, but copper, steel and aluminium cannot be hedged directly. PSU contracts are fixed price.

qa_highlights.question: BESS margins at EBITDA and PAT level.
qa_highlights.answer: NTPC BESS project expected at around 10% PAT margin (fixed contract); two IPP BESS projects (GUVNL and RRVUNL) targeted at minimum IRR of about 16%.

qa_highlights.question: Why annual report disclosure on procurement/pass-through differs from the guided margin cut from 10.5% to 6-7%.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NTPC LOA came 4-5 months after L1 (Oct 2025 bid, Feb-March 2026 LOA), so pre-procurement was not possible; bid validity of 120-180 days limits steps. It said the margin guidance has been cut because of metal price spikes.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in achieving FY27 guidance, given H1 revenue of Rs 1,369 crore (as stated in call) and guidance of Rs 1,600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 is typically much stronger (H2 FY26 about Rs 100 crore against H1 about Rs 20 crore as stated) and it is fairly confident of meeting the revenue and margin targets.

qa_highlights.question: Solar cell JV technology, internal versus external utilisation, and asset-light model.
qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon technology; 70-80% of capacity to be used internally (60-70% per a later answer) and 15-20% to be sold externally; management said it remains asset-light and will not scale manufacturing beyond ETC needs.

risks_watch: Metal price volatility on fixed-price PSU contracts; management expects a decline in copper and steel from January 2027 but this is unconfirmed.
Margin guidance cut twice (from 10.5% to 5-7%); credibility of FY28 Rs 3,000 crore revenue target and Rs 200-220 crore tax outlook.
Export approvals and Chinese restrictions on solar cell and BESS equipment; cell JV timing (June 2027) at risk.
Working capital and cash flow, given heavy H2 revenue weighting and deferred procurement.
Possible NTPC REL L1 confirmation for two orders worth about Rs 1,271 crore expected in November or early December 2026.
Decision on 2 GWh lithium-ion cell plant due by end-December 2026 or mid-December; China export restrictions cited.
Shareholder action plan promised for the current quarter, including whether any buyback is announced.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth and FY28 targets but openly cautious on FY27 margins, attributing the shortfall to metal prices and delayed LOAs. Answers on shareholder returns and the margin guidance cut were less specific, with the board promising a later update.
key_quotes: So we believe FY27 margins will remain under strain. FY28 should be a bumper year for solar world.
The board has taken the feedback very, very seriously.
Our motto is that we should be India leading backward integrated ETC company and not a leading manufacturer.

growth.why: FY27 guided to revenue of Rs 1,600-1,700 crore (cut, per the brief's 'around 6000 crores' quote being inconsistent) and EBITDA margin 5-7% (6-7% cited), backed by Rs 3,856 crore order book and commissioned BESS/module lines, though the brief's Q2 revenue figure of Rs 2,244 crore is internally inconsistent and the 77% growth claim is unverified; FY28 target of ~Rs 3,000 crore rests on order book an

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management still targets 6-7% FY27 EBITDA margin (H1 at 8.3%, Q2 at 5.9%) and says material costs normalise to last year's share of revenue in H2; new orders at higher prices and solar cell/module margins guided 15-20%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 2.4 GW TOPCon cell JV at Narmadapuram is under construction with commercial production targeted June 2027 and first equity tranche of Rs 26.8 crore already paid on Oct 30, 2026; 1.5 GW module plant and BESS factory already commissioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 order execution guided at Rs 1,100-1,200 crore with Rs 2,600 crore carried into FY28, and FY28 revenue target of about Rs 3,000 crore; but FY27 revenue guide of Rs 1,600-1,700 crore is cut and H1 is reported as Rs 412 crore, so the H2 ramp is steep.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Decision on a 2 GWh lithium-ion cell plant in India is due by end-December 2026, but PLI application was withdrawn and management says it will not scale manufacturing beyond ETC needs; utilisation not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue and margin guidance were cut twice (margin from 10.5% to 5-7%), and the FY28 Rs 3,000 crore target rests on an order book with only about Rs 2,600 crore carried into FY28.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 margin was 8.3% and Q2 5.9%, the FY27 6-7% target needs H2 recovery, and management is relying on metal prices easing from Jan 2027 which is unconfirmed; the brief's Q2 revenue figure is internally inconsistent, so the base is unverified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Solar cell (TOPCon) output from the JV is targeted for June 2027 and a 2 GWh lithium-ion cell plant is under evaluation with a decision by end-December 2026; neither is a firm product launch in the window.

rows.label: NTPC REL L1 confirmation on orders worth about Rs 1,271 crore
rows.why: Confirmation of two orders worth about Rs 1,271 crore is expected in November or early December 2026, which would add to the Rs 3,856 crore order book.

rows.label: Board shareholder-value action (possible buyback)
rows.why: Board said it will return to shareholders in the current quarter with short-term actions, but no buyback was confirmed and it was raised by an investor.

rows.label: Metal price normalisation lifts margins
rows.why: Management expects copper and steel to decline from January 2027, which would help margins on fixed-price PSU contracts, but this is unconfirmed and PSU tenders have no pass-through.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY28 targets (a 'bumper year') and the JV timeline but cautious on FY27 margins, blaming metal spikes and delayed LOAs; analysts pressed on the twice-cut margin guidance, the Rs 200-300 crore PAT promise and the buyback question, which management left unconfirmed.
